name: Sydney
summary: Central Sydney: 7,962 buildings, the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, sun access on protected public places, and a game: walk it, ride the ferries, fly under the bridge.

guide.line: A harbour city of sails and sandstone. Take the ferry past the Opera House, wander The Rocks where the colony began, and watch the bridge light up as the sun goes down behind Balmain.
spots: Utzon's white sails on Bennelong Point
The Coathanger: fly beneath its steel arch
Green-and-gold ferries out to Manly and Taronga
local: Local
Gadigal Country for tens of thousands of years. Today: a flat white at dawn, a ferry to work, fish and chips on the quay.

name: Marunouchi & Ginza
summary: Marunouchi to Tokyo Tower: 15,000 buildings, 76% of the footprint area at a PLATEAU-surveyed height, Tokyo Tower built to its published dimensions, and a game: Tokyo Station, the Palace, Hibiya Park, the water bus and a helicopter to the tower.
tagline: Tokyo Station, the Palace, Ginza, the water bus and Tokyo Tower

group_meta.summary: Tokyo as maps, the way games draw it: each district a walkable map of its own, chosen from the subway map. Lit stations are built; grey ones are next.
group_meta.note: Districts and lines from the Tokyo Metro and JR East maps; station positions are the stations' own (OpenStreetMap). Which districts a game sends you to follows Persona 5's Tokyo (Atlus, 2016): Shibuya, Shinjuku, Akihabara, Asakusa, Ueno, Ikebukuro, Odaiba, Jinbocho, Kanda, Tsukishima.

guide.line: Red-brick Tokyo Station, glass towers and the moats and stone walls of the Imperial Palace.
Tokyo's grand boulevard: flagship stores, Wako's clock tower and the water bus down to Tokyo Tower.

name: Whitsundays
summary: The Whitsunday Islands and the inner Great Barrier Reef: 30 m survey bathymetry, a Sentinel-2 sea floor, caustics, wet sand and a swash line. Walk Whitehaven Beach, snorkel, dive.
tagline: Whitehaven Beach, Hill Inlet and the Whitsunday Passage

guide.hook: Whitehaven's pure silica sand swirling into the turquoise of Hill Inlet

group_meta.summary: Five sites on the Great Barrier Reef, rebuilt from survey bathymetry and satellite imagery under the real sun, moon and tide. Walk, snorkel, dive, sail and fly.

guide.line: The largest living thing on Earth: 2,300 km of coral off Queensland. Swim with turtles, walk silica sand as white as snow, and fly over Heart Reef.
local: Reef manners
Reef-safe sunscreen, fins kept off the coral, and a turtle always has right of way.

name: Hardy Reef
tagline: Heart Reef and the Reefworld pontoon, outer reef
summary: Hardy Reef on the outer Great Barrier Reef: Heart Reef, the Reefworld pontoon on the channel wall, and Hook, Line and Bait reefs, from 30 m survey bathymetry and Sentinel-2. No land: start on the pontoon's deck and dive the wall.

guide.hook: Heart Reef from the air, the outer reef from the pontoon

name: Green Island
tagline: Coral cay off Cairns, with Arlington Reef and Michaelmas Cay

guide.hook: A rainforest cay off Cairns: snorkel straight off the beach

tagline: The southernmost coral cay of the reef

guide.hook: Manta rays gliding at the reef's southern tip

name: Lake Pukaki
tagline: Aoraki / Mount Cook over the glacial-blue lake
summary: Lake Pukaki and Aoraki / Mount Cook, 38 by 84 km of the Mackenzie: LINZ's 1 m LiDAR terrain and aerial photos, the lake's glacial-flour blue measured from Sentinel-2, tussock and lupins, a sky from physical scattering and the dark-sky reserve's stars. Walk from Peter's Lookout, fly round Aoraki, walk the Hooker Valley.

guide.hook: Aoraki / Mount Cook over a lake of glacial milk-blue

group_meta.summary: Two glacial lakes of the Mackenzie Basin on LINZ's 1 m LiDAR terrain and aerial photos: Lake Pukaki under Aoraki / Mount Cook, and Lake Tekapo with the Church of the Good Shepherd, under the dark-sky reserve's stars.

guide.line: Glacier-blue lakes under New Zealand's highest peak, and a night sky so dark it's protected as a reserve for the stars.
local: Local
Lupins in early summer, the Milky Way overhead, and silence at the Church of the Good Shepherd.

name: Lake Tekapo
tagline: The Church of the Good Shepherd on the turquoise lake
summary: Lake Tekapo / Takapō, 36 by 52 km of the Mackenzie: LINZ's 1 m LiDAR terrain and aerial photos, the Church of the Good Shepherd, the sheepdog statue and Mt John's observatory modelled from the survey, lupins in their season and the dark-sky reserve's stars. Start at the church's postcard view, climb Mt John, find the Southern Cross.

guide.hook: A little stone church on the turquoise shore, under the stars

name: Milford Sound
tagline: Mitre Peak a mile out of the sea, and a ship under the falls
summary: Milford Sound / Piopiotahi, 20 by 20 km of Fiordland: the fiord from the Tasman Sea to the Cleddau on LINZ's open terrain and imagery, rainforest on walls a kilometre high, Stirling Falls with a rainbow in its spray, fair-weather cumulus, gulls, lupins on the river flats, and a 40 m ship that sails the day cruise's line. Ride her out under Mitre Peak.

guide.hook: A ship under mile-high walls, a waterfall straight into the sea
guide.line: The fiord Kipling called the eighth wonder: Mitre Peak rising 1,690 m straight from the water, rainforest clinging to the rock, and falls that never stop.
spots: 1,690 m straight out of the fiord
151 m into the sea, a rainbow in its spray
Ride the ship out to the Tasman Sea
local: Local
Rata in flower at Christmas, a rainbow in the spray of Stirling Falls, and gulls behind the boat.

guide.line: The city that never sleeps: Lower Manhattan's canyons, the Statue of Liberty across the harbour, and a slice at midnight.
